title: Your first ultralearning project
coreMove: Choose a first project serious enough to deserve protected time and small enough to start cleanly.
sourcePressure: A first project should be hard enough to matter, concrete enough to guide action, and protected enough to compete for time. The source sidecar contains no named people, studies, institutions, places, dates, or artifacts for this chapter, so named source anchors must be omitted rather than invented.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Calling a vague intention a project or choosing a heroic scope that cannot survive the first week.

hook: Ch13: learner stares at browser tabs and realizes motivation is not enough
Ch13: broad modern world pressure opener
counterintuition: The obvious move is not the real move
Most people think more effort is enough
This is not about working harder
tryThisNow: Spend one minute thinking about your learning journey
examples: desk plus laptop plus vague course collection
manager in a recurring meeting with no concrete artifact

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: Emma, a customer-support manager choosing a first analytics project
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who has been mistaking motion for progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the next month produces visible evidence or another private feeling of effort
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Emma chooses one customer-support analytics project with a weekly block and one dashboard that will prove the skill.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a support-ticket export beside a hand-drawn dashboard grid

exampleSpecs.domain: Matthew, a biology student protecting time for one lab-technique sprint
exampleSpecs.audience: a practitioner under a near-term performance constraint
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a deadline exposes the weakness early enough to adjust
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Matthew protects two lab-technique sessions before buying more biology materials, then names the first observable pass.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pipette calibration card beside a taped lab schedule

exampleSpecs.domain: Vincent, a school counsellor scoping a trauma-informed training project
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who has been mistaking motion for progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the learner keeps credibility with a reviewer, client, teacher, or team
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Vincent scopes trauma-informed training to one supervision scenario instead of an entire counselling identity.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a supervision-room chair beside a printed scenario sheet

exampleSpecs.domain: Isabel, a printmaker making the goal serious enough to deserve studio hours
exampleSpecs.audience: a practitioner under a near-term performance constraint
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the project survives contact with a real schedule and real standards
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Isabel makes the printmaking project serious by reserving studio hours and defining a six-print proof set.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: six blank deckle-edge sheets stacked by an ink roller

exampleSpecs.domain: Devon, a cloud-admin apprentice defining the first deployable artifact
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who has been mistaking motion for progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether comfort keeps protecting the exact skill gap that matters
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Devon names the first deployable cloud artifact and refuses to call the project started until it runs.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a server diagram sketched on a whiteboard with one arrow missing

exampleSpecs.domain: Maja, a city volunteer turning a climate-data interest into a scoped project
exampleSpecs.audience: a practitioner under a near-term performance constraint
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the next attempt changes the skill instead of decorating the plan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Maja turns climate-data interest into a scoped volunteer map with a due date and a named reviewer.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a community-centre bulletin board with a blank map pin

skillTargets: choose a first project with protected time and concrete direction
turn commitment into a startable plan

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
